_fixture_meta.verification: scripts/10_verify_calibration_output.py reopens every declared raster and asserts pixel size, origin, shape, EPSG GeoKey, nodata tag, dtype, real-georeference flag and valid-pixel count, then feeds the array into the real heightfield_to_mesh() consumer.
_fixture_meta.why_not_v1: Rolled back from a premature v1. The export mechanism is implemented and round-trip tested, but at the time of the first freeze it had only been exercised on synthetic arrays and on the ground-truth Vaihingen raster -- NOT on real model predictions -- and no downstream consumer had reviewed the field set. HANDOFF_INTERFACE_POLICY's v1 bar is 'downstream teammates are allowed to build against it', which needs real validation plus consumer review, neither of which had happened. Flagged by Anmol in the Day-1 review and accepted: freezing on mechanism alone was the wrong call.

scripts/10_verify_calibration_output.py passing against those real rasters

embedded_tags.34735 GeoKeyDirectoryTag: GTModelType=1 projected, GTRasterType=1 PixelIsArea, ProjectedCSType=32767 (USER-DEFINED), ProjLinearUnits=9001 metre

epsg.meaning: GeoTIFF user-defined CRS. No authority code is asserted.
epsg.WARNING: The pixel grid and geotransform are real and round-trip exactly; the ABSOLUTE CRS is not asserted. Earlier exports stamped EPSG:32633, taken from the dataset's own dsm.vrt (PROJCS['WGS 84 / UTM zone 33N'], per PHASE2_RED_FLAGS/02_DATASET_RESEARCH.md). That code is wrong: easting 496794.825 implies longitude ~8.96E under UTM 32N, which is Vaihingen, whereas under 33N the same easting implies ~14.96E, about 600 km east. Rather than substitute 32632 or 25832 - our arithmetic against the source's own declaration, still unverified - we assert no authority code at all. A consumer needing a real CRS must establish it independently.

calibration.WARNING: per_tile_full_oracle and per_scene_oracle_scale_shift are calibrated against the tile's own dense ground truth: a NON-DEPLOYABLE upper bound. sparse_10 is deployment-like but still samples the test tile. Neither is a blind generalization figure. Do not strip the manifest's IMPORTANT field when quoting any number derived from these.

extent.note: 04_make_patches.py drops patches failing its validity mask, so 07's rasters can be sparse inside their bounding extent; uncovered pixels are nodata.

error_behavior.epsg_required: no default; a georeferenced product is never written by falling through a default
error_behavior.guessed_georeference: save_dsm_geotiff(require_georeferenced=True) raises when the source transform came from load_geotiff's Vaihingen nominal fallback rather than real data
error_behavior.missing_tfw: both producers SKIP the export and record the reason in their manifest rather than writing a guessed georeference
error_behavior.strict_load: load_geotiff(path, strict=True) raises instead of guessing

consumer_must_know: Elevation is absolute in the GeoTIFF but REBASED in the mesh: heightfield_to_mesh computes Z = (elev - elev.min()) * z_exaggeration, so the .glb loses the datum. Add elev.min() back from the GeoTIFF if true height is needed. See pipeline_to_3d_v1.json z_computation.
Mask nodata BEFORE meshing - -9999 pixels drag the mesh floor down through that same elev.min() rebase. scripts/10_verify_calibration_output.py shows the pattern.
Read gsd from GeoRaster.gsd. K3_mesh_pipeline.py currently hardcodes gsd=0.09.

real_verified_round_trip_result.note: Geometry contract identical to K2's verified run; save_geotiff reuses K2's exact tag construction. Re-verified for calibrated predictions by scripts/10_verify_calibration_output.py, whose report lands at outputs/metrics/calibration_output_consumer_check.json.
